title: Piano Concerto No. 2, Moderato: Rachmaninoff and Richter
work: Piano Concerto No. 2, Op. 18 — I. Moderato, opening-side comparison only
question: Rachmaninoff and Richter play the opening chords, the running accompaniment beneath the first theme and the piano’s second theme in E♭ major.
intro: The piano opens with a series of chords, then moves into running notes beneath a melody for strings and clarinet. Later the soloist plays a theme of its own in E♭ major. Rachmaninoff’s 1929 Philadelphia performance and Richter’s 1959 Warsaw recording are compared here over the opening disc side.

recordings.label: Rachmaninoff, Stokowski, Philadelphia Orchestra, 1929
recordings.note: Recorded at Philadelphia’s Academy of Music on 10 April 1929; the published opening comes from the third take.

recordings.label: Richter, Wisłocki, Warsaw Philharmonic, 1959
recordings.note: Richter and Wisłocki made this complete concerto recording with the Warsaw Philharmonic for Deutsche Grammophon.

passages.label: First theme in C minor, strings
passages.note: Violins, violas and clarinet play the C minor tune. The piano plays broken chords beneath them, above pizzicato cellos and basses.

passages.label: Piano figuration over woodwind chords
passages.note: The piano, until now beneath the strings, plays running figures between held woodwind chords and short orchestral replies.

passages.label: Second theme in E♭ major
passages.note: The piano plays the second theme in E♭ major above its own broken chords. Quiet strings and short wind phrases accompany it.
